subject: Post-call: Long-context eval & next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Long-context eval & next steps (Acme)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

TL;DR
- Redwood will run a focused long-context eval on a sample of your documents (you to share sample doc + doc stats)
- We'll test 3 model variants (base long-window model, quantized 4-bit variant, and our extended-context tuned model)
- Deliverable: evaluation report with truncation behavior, summarization fidelity metrics, and recommended config

What we heard from you:
- Primary goal: reliably summarize/condense multi-section technical documents (avg length ~30–60k tokens; some up to ~150k) without losing key action items
- Pain: current system truncates important end-of-doc sections; summaries lose context for timelines and action owners
- Constraints: data residency in US, strong compliance needs (SOC2/PCI may be relevant), and throughput requirement ~50 reqs/min at p95 latency < 3s for summaries

Proposed evaluation plan (high-level):
1) You share: 3 representative documents (anonymized) + a short prompt set (we can use attached prompt set as starting point) — see acme_long_context_prompt_set_v1.txt
2) Redwood runs: redwood-extended-1.0 (long-window), redwood-extended-1.0-4q (4-bit quantized), and open-extended-v1 baseline
3) Metrics: truncation rate by token position, ROUGE/LUKE-style factuality checks for named entities and timelines, human-eval sampling for action-item fidelity
4) Timeframe: initial report in ~3 business days after sample receipt; deeper runs + tuning ~10 business days

Attachments: acme_long_context_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompt set), redwood_benchmark_report_q3_2026.pdf (our recent long-context benchmarks)

Next steps / asks for you:
- Please confirm you can share 3 anonymized docs and whether we should expect redaction prior to upload
- Any additional compliance contacts (SOC 2 / security) we should include on future threads?
- Preference for meeting to review results: next Tue/Wed?

Thanks — will kick off once we get the samples.

—

Great — thanks Jordan. Answers below and next steps.

On "truncation rate by token position":
- We split docs into token positions and track what fraction of summaries miss content originating from tokens in the last X% of the document. For example, if action items are frequently in the final 10% and the model omits them, that shows up as a high truncation-impact score for tail tokens. We'll produce a chart showing factual misses vs. token percentile.

On quantization vs. full models:
- In our benchmarks (see attached redwood_benchmark_report_q3_2026.pdf) the 4-bit quantized variants have ~5–8% lower factuality on very long, highly technical docs compared to full 16-bit runs, but latency and throughput improve materially (2–3x throughput improvement in dedicated settings). We'll surface a recommended fallback policy (use quantized for background/less-critical summaries; full model for legal/compliance summaries).

On throughput for dedicated capacity:
- Yes, with Redwood Dedicated and our autoscaling config we can meet ~50 reqs/min p95 for long-window runs on a moderate reserved pool (we'll size this as part of the evaluation). Michael and Dev are cc'd to scope the capacity estimate and expected cost impact.

Secure upload: please use the shared S3 link we provide (expiring). I'm attaching the upload instructions and will create a one-time secure upload link after you confirm which doc you want to send first.

Planned deliverables/timeline after sample receipt:
- Day 0 (receipt): smoke test + tokenization report
- Day 1–2: run three model variants and compute truncation/factuality metrics + automated evaluation
- Day 3: summary report + recommended model/config and suggested rollout/fallback policy

I'll also link the evaluation notebook and Drive folder after Dev creates the upload bucket.

Thanks — look forward to the samples.

—
Marissa Cole

Hi Jordan — Dev from Redwood SE team here. Quick technical notes to set expectations and what we'd like with the samples: 

What we'll measure (technical):
- Tokenization profile: token counts per document and distribution (we need the original file text ideally)
- Truncation simulation: we run summarization with and without truncation windows to see where summaries drop content
- Chunking & stitching: for very long docs we'll evaluate both single-pass long-context (where model supports it) and chunk+stitch approaches with overlap (recommended overlap 512–1k tokens)
- KV cache impact: we'll measure inference cost when prefix caching is enabled for repeated sections across docs (helps for templates)

Preferred sample format: plain text (.txt) or Markdown. PDF is OK but text extraction can alter token counts — if you must send PDF, include a plain-text version as well.

Suggested inference configs we will try (examples):
- redwood-extended-1.0: max_context=131072, chunking=none, temp=0.0 for extractive summaries
- redwood-extended-1.0-4q: max_context=131072, chunking=none, temp=0.0 (note: quantized variant may show more hallucinations on numeric tables)
- chunk+stitch baseline: chunk_size=16k, overlap=1k, stitch_strategy=lead-weighted

If you can upload one ~50k doc (text) and one ~120k doc (text), that's ideal. We'll run the tokenization and send back the initial plots by EOD tomorrow after we receive files.

—
Dev Patel
